judgements.justification: B's area chair gave the oral with no reason beyond quoting Reviewer_rfa1's 'clear, rigorous, and well written' (the lone 9 against four 7s) and named none of the weaknesses that Reviewer_1SfX, Reviewer_4Bw1 and Reviewer_3m9X raised.
No calibration gap: both committees wrote similar verdicts at the same scores, and without Reviewer_rfa1's 9 B's mean is 7.0, exactly A's.
B's oral did not rest on agreement: B had a 9 above the accept level, and its meta-review cites no unanimity.
B's raises rested on the identifiability argument, the xor example and clarifications; A saw the same complexity answer, so B's raises did not rest on evidence A lacked.

B's meta-review quotes Reviewer_rfa1 and Reviewer_3m9X and mentions no weakness, though its reviewers called the paper dense and the experiments artificial; A's meta-review kept 'the main shortcoming of the paper is its clarity'.
Reviewer_N9bU's misreading of the theory as binary set no final score: N9bU rose to 7 and A's area chair did not repeat it.
The authors' concessions to A (a metric typo, an axis label, a missing citation) are presentation fixes, not unfavourable facts about the results.
Reviewer_rfa1 posted late, but with a positive 9, not a new objection; no late objection stood unanswered.
The scores were not near-identical: B's tier rests on Reviewer_rfa1's 9, a difference in the reviews, not on a different cut-off for the same scores.
B's highest-confidence reviewer, Reviewer_rfa1 (confidence 4), is the one B's chair followed; A's chair cited Reviewer_aRng, A's most detailed critic.
Concerns overlapped heavily and the rebuttal moved scores on both committees (N9bU in A; 1SfX and 3m9X in B); A's main concern, clarity, was raised in B too.
Reviewer_rfa1's 9 against four 7s lifts B's mean from 7.0 to 7.4, and without it B's scores match A's mean of 7.0.
Reviewer_rfa1 skipped the discussion, but the response did not answer any basis of the 9, so non-engagement kept no answered score in place.
Neither committee had a low outlier that its area chair discarded; A's lowest score, aRng's 6, was cited, not set aside.
No reviewer or area chair raised audience breadth or venue fit; density for readers outside causality was raised on both sides as clarity.
Neither meta-review misreported the reviewers' final positions or the rebuttal; B's omitted weaknesses (R14) but stated nothing false.
Most reviewers on both committees replied to the response; in B only Reviewer_rfa1 did not.
B's confidence-1 reviewers (nWYc, 4Bw1) rated 7, below the confident reviewers' mean, so counting them did not lift B; A also counted N9bU's confidence-1 7.
Neither committee split between accept and reject; every rating was in the accept range.
Stage 1 finds no difference in substance between the authors' responses; both got the same complexity bound.
No novelty verdict rested on wrong prior work; the de Haan et al. (2019) omission was conceded as orthogonal, and Reviewer_rfa1 did not assess novelty.
B's meta-review only says 'It is my pleasure to recommend acceptance' and gives no reason for an oral over four 7s and one 9.
Reviewer_1SfX's objection to the strict imitation target was answered and 1SfX raised to 7; no framing objection counted against the paper.
B's champion, Reviewer_rfa1, gave a generic review and did not engage, so B had no closely engaged champion; A's Reviewer_WPhA gave a specific 8.
No committee rejected the paper over the size of promised revisions; both accepted it.
Both area chairs relied only on the visible reviews.
Both committees valued the paper as a theoretical contribution; neither demanded a different kind of contribution.
No below-threshold score held: Reviewer_aRng's 6 is in the accept range and rests on clarity, which A's chair called the main shortcoming.
